issues.legal_issue: Members of an unlawful assembly are not liable for murder when the common object was to cause injuries likely to cause death, but the common object was not to cause death or commit murder and no individually attributable injury establishes murder liability.
material_facts: The accused attacked the deceased, a close family member, during an unexpected quarrel arising from a dispute over water rights.

The deceased suffered 27 injuries, mostly simple injuries to non-vital areas; two injuries involved a finger fracture, and the court found that no attacker intended to cause death or an injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
Although the doctor stated that the injuries were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, the court was not satisfied that the injuries were cumulatively sufficient on that basis.
The court found that the assembly's common object was to cause bodily injuries likely to cause death, rather than to cause death or commit murder.
issues.conclusion: The murder conviction was set aside and the accused were found guilty of culpable homicide punishable under section 304(1) read with section 149 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 300(iii) of the Indian Penal Code, intentionally inflicting bodily injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death constitutes murder. For liability under section 302 read with section 149, the prosecution must establish that the murder was committed in prosecution of the unlawful assembly's common object, or that the members knew murder was likely to be committed in prosecution of that object. Where a fatal injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature is attributable to an individual accused, that accused may be liable under section 302 without section 149; where the alleged sufficiency rests on the cumulative effect of injuries, the common object or the members' knowledge must support murder liability. On these facts, the common object was to cause injuries likely to cause death, an offence punishable under section 304(1). No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction and unlawful_assembly_caused_death and common_object_injuries_likely_to_cause_death and not common_object_to_cause_death_or_commit_murder and fatal_injury_not_individually_attributed

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for murder.
predicates.unlawful_assembly_caused_death: Members of an unlawful assembly attacked a person, and the person died from the resulting injuries.
predicates.common_object_injuries_likely_to_cause_d: The assembly's common object was to cause bodily injuries likely to cause death.
predicates.common_object_to_cause_death_or_commit_m: The assembly's common object was to cause death or commit murder, or its members knew murder was likely in pursuing that object.
predicates.fatal_injury_not_individually_attributed: No accused was shown to have intentionally inflicted an injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.

issues.definition: When an unlawful assembly's attack causes death, but its common object was only to inflict injuries likely to cause death and neither murder intent or knowledge nor an individually attributable murder-level injury is established, the murder conviction is replaced with a culpable-homicide conviction.

issues.legal_issue: A sentencing court may direct compensation to a person who suffered loss or injury, or to eligible dependants, and must assess the suitability and amount of compensation in light of the offender's ability to pay and the relevant circumstances.
material_facts: The deceased's dependants, including his widow, had suffered loss as a result of his death.
The court found that the accused had sufficient funds to compensate the dependants at least to some extent.

The court considered the nature of the crime, the injury suffered, the justness of the compensation claim, the accused's capacity to pay, and other relevant circumstances, and directed that the fine imposed be paid to the widow as compensation.
issues.conclusion: The court imposed a fine on each accused and directed that the fine be paid as compensation to the deceased's widow.
issues.legal_principle: Section 357(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 allows a court, when imposing a sentence that does not include a fine, to order payment of compensation to a person who suffered loss or injury. The provision advances the purpose of compensating those entitled to recover damages from the offender, extending beyond the earlier power under section 545 of the 1898 Code to pay compensation out of a fine. Before awarding compensation, the court must decide whether the case is suitable and assess the offender's capacity to pay; an order is ineffective if the offender cannot pay. In fixing a fine or compensation, the court must consider the nature of the crime, the injury, the justness of the claim, capacity to pay, and other relevant circumstances, rather than first selecting compensation and then setting a higher fine. The court relied on Palaniappa Gounder v. State of Tamil Nadu.

rule.if: criminal_sentencing_after_conviction and eligible_recipient_suffered_loss_or_injury and compensation_case_is_fit and offender_can_pay and relevant_circumstances_assessed

predicates.criminal_sentencing_after_conviction: The court is determining the consequences of a criminal conviction at sentencing.
predicates.eligible_recipient_suffered_loss_or_inju: A person entitled to receive compensation, including an injured person or eligible dependant, suffered loss or injury because of the offender's act.
predicates.compensation_case_is_fit: The court determined that the circumstances make the case suitable for an award of compensation.
predicates.offender_can_pay: The court found that the offender has the capacity to pay compensation.
predicates.relevant_circumstances_assessed: The court considered the nature of the crime, the injury or loss, the fairness of the claim, the offender's capacity to pay, and other relevant circumstances.

issues.definition: When sentencing follows a conviction, an eligible recipient has suffered loss or injury, compensation is suitable, the offender can pay, and the relevant circumstances have been assessed, compensation is awarded to the eligible recipient.
